newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says stable Asia currency needed.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says stable Asia currency needed.

text.p: A major Japanese news agency reported on Friday that its Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto believes a stable currency is needed in Asia so that the region can keep up with global trading.
In a meeting with Japanese reporters at his official residence, to which foreign news organisations did not have access, Kyodo News Agency said:

"Hashimoto indicated the government is planning to revise the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law as part of Japan's 'Big Bang' financial reform, which is modelled on Britain's sweeping financial system transformation of 1986."

"The prime minister stressed that to ensure a stable yen, a drastic change is needed, including abolition of the current system, whereby banks need to be authorized by the Finance Ministry to engage in foreign exchange trading," Kyodo reported.

"He pointed out that in the future, the Euro currency, scheduled to be launched in 1999, will emerge as a key reserve currency in addition to the U.S. dollar, and that global trading will be based on these two currencies," Kyodo said.
"With its current conditions, Japan will not be able to keep up with the world. And there will be disorder without a stable currency in Asia," Kyodo quoted the prime minister as saying.
